references.text: The author draws a direct parallel between Moses as a servant in God's house and Christ as the Son over the house. This is a theological elaboration of the contrast between the servant's temporary position and the Son's eternal position in John 8:35.

Here David is called God's firstborn and exalted above the kings of the earth, with an eternal throne. This underscores the theme of the Son's eternal right to dwell in God's house, as opposed to the servant's temporary role.

John writes that those who received Jesus became children of God, while Jesus himself is the only begotten Son. This connects to the theme of the Son's unique and eternal place in God's house, as opposed to the servant's place.
